title: Launch templates and auto scaling groups

videos.script: An instance you launch by hand is a pet. You name it, you fix it, and you worry about it. {{pet}} This lesson replaces it with two things. A launch template writes down what one machine is: the image, the type, the disk, the tags. And it keeps every version you ever wrote, numbered, and never changed. {{versions}} Then an auto scaling group takes that template and a number. Three, say. It launches three. From then on it compares the number with what exists. One instance fails its health check? It is terminated, and another one is launched. Nobody logs in. {{group}} You will build both against moto, on your own laptop. And you will see where moto is kinder than AWS. It accepts a count above the maximum. It puts every instance in one zone. It marks an instance unhealthy and leaves it running. Each time, the lesson says what AWS would do instead. {{zones}} The last part is the one people get wrong. A new template version changes nothing that is already running. Rolling it through the group is a separate act, called an instance refresh, and it takes longer than you think. {{refresh}}
